commit_evidence: tag v1.5.0 points at the commit, and the npm SLSA provenance of the 1.5.0 tarball (built from refs/tags/v1.5.0) names it
scope: coding-agent product fork only; lower agent/provider layers unchanged

npm_distribution.relation: The worker installs the npm registry tarball of the same 1.5.0 release built from the pinned commit. Its package.json is byte-identical to upstream/package.json (hash in files). From 1.0 pi publishes no npm-shrinkwrap.json: the tarball pins its direct dependencies exactly, and upstream pins the transitive tree only in packages/coding-agent/install-lock/ (the lockfile its installer uses), retained here as upstream/install-lock/. The worker's lockfile resolves the SDK's dependency closure to exactly that install lock (names, versions, resolved URLs and integrity; the lockstep pi packages, which upstream records without integrity, carry their registry integrity), and npm hoists it, so pi-ai is installed once at node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai (packages/pi-worker/test/worker-deps.test.ts). With the empty patch inventory this registry tarball is the narrow fork's runnable distribution. Unpatched; only root exports are imported, plus pi-ai's root entry from the one installed copy (src/worker/pi-ai.ts).
npm_distribution.install: npm --prefix packages/pi-worker ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund (the skipped install scripts are protobufjs's version-scheme warning and @google/genai's no-op preinstall, none needed by the worker; see docs/implementation/build.md)

@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent.use: SDK root exports: createAgentSession, ModelRuntime, SessionManager, SettingsManager, DefaultResourceLoader; the pi-ai root entry it resolves (createAssistantMessageEventStream, getCurrentSystemPrompt, getSupportedThinkingLevels, stream types) for the lade-fixture provider and the catalogue, and normalizeContext for the dependency test

undici.use: global dispatcher tunnelling through the LADE gateway socket; the same version the SDK pins
